stage1.impression: A competent, warm, low-key render of a timber-lined bar. The tonality is believable, but the large surfaces are too clean and too evenly lit: flat veneer doors, a terrazzo floor and counter front that read as speckled carpet or cork, four identical stools and four identical tables, and no sign of life beyond a few glasses. The amber band under the ceiling reads as a printed, corrugated strip with moire, not glowing cast acrylic, and a stray diagonal haze shaft cuts across it. As it stands a magazine would see a generic hotel-lobby bar, not a specific, well-made place. It reads as CG.

blocking_9: The acrylic band must read as thick lit fins: polished edges glowing, depth between fins, no moire, and the brightest designed element in the frame (band lum_p95 >= 180, with fins resolved)
The lantern must read as the destination: a visible foot line of light under the box and porch separating it from the floor, and the porch shown as a porch with depth, not flush veneer doors
Terrazzo at 1:1 must read as honed stone (chips in proportion, a polished sheen catching the counter and pendant light), not carpet or cork
The counter must be the lit pool of the room: quartzite top median 60 or more with visible stone veining and specular, the bottles and glasses catching small highlights
Life in the frame: motion-blurred guests at the counter or banquette, a bartender, records or a coat, so it is not an empty showroom
No repeated identical props in a row (stools, tables, glasses), and no CG artefacts (fireflies in the band, the diagonal haze shaft, the rigid throw on the banquette)

defects.what: Amber acrylic band reads as a flat printed or corrugated strip: left half flat orange, right half fine fins with moire, no glowing edges; median 85, p95 137, so it is not a light source
Stray diagonal light shaft (haze-lit beam) slashing from the ceiling across the band; reads as a lens or render artefact, with no source
Two bright specks on the band (fireflies or stray specular dots)
Porch reads as two flat veneer doors with a perfectly uniform grain and a hard grazing hotspot at the top (profile 132 to 39 top to bottom); no depth, no hardware detail, no wear
No visible foot line under the lantern despite foot line 9.0; base median 35, the box sits on the floor with no light gap
Counter front terrazzo reads as multicoloured speckle or cork board, chips oversized and saturated (red and green flecks), median 20
Terrazzo floor reads as carpet or gravel: fine noisy granular texture, no honed sheen, no reflection of the lights
Quartzite bar top is a dull flat dark grey (median 41) with no veining or specular; under 4 x 90 W spots it should be the brightest pool
Four identical stools, evenly spaced, identical heights: repeated copies of one model
Four identical black tables in a perfect row with near-identical glasses; showroom staging
Throw over the banquette is a rigid flat board, no drape or folds
Right wall is a featureless dark plane (median 18), no plaster texture or any light pool
Hard-edged diagonal shadow across the slatted baffle with no believable occluder; slats perfectly uniform with no grain variation
No people, no motion blur, no records: the frame reads as empty

changes.problem: The acrylic band, the room's signature, reads as a flat printed strip rather than glowing thick fins.

evidence.measured: lum_median 85.2, lum_p95 137.3, no clipping; left half flat orange, right half moire fins; less bright than the porch's hotspot (132)

change.to: 0.25 (with the fins in a clearer Smoke so their polished edges catch the glow)

changes.expected: The band becomes the brightest designed element, with the fin edges reading as bright lines against darker faces and a soft amber spill onto the ceiling and the top of the baffle.

changes.problem: The counter, which should be the room's main pool of light, is a dull grey slab.

evidence.measured: lum_median 40.6, p95 94; quartzite shows no veining or specular

change.to: 160 W, 20 deg, aimed to land pools on the top in front of each stool, and a higher quartzite reflection (honed, roughness about 0.3)

changes.expected: Pools of light on the bar top with highlights on the glasses and the stone; the counter reads first on the left.

changes.problem: The lantern's foot line is not visible, so the box does not read as a freestanding object on its own floor.

evidence.measured: lum_median 35.2, crush_pct 2.2; no lit line in the crop

change.to: 30, and check that it is not occluded by the floor or the porch base

changes.expected: A thin warm line of light under the lantern and porch that lifts the box off the terrazzo and reflects softly in the floor.

changes.problem: The frame is empty, so it reads as a showroom rather than a bar at night.

evidence.measured: people: 0 figures; only five glasses on the counter and two on the tables

change.to: 3 to 4 motion-blurred figures (two seated at the counter, a bartender behind it, a couple on the banquette), shutter about 1/8 s; add a record out of its sleeve and a coat over a stool

changes.expected: Signs of life with no faces shown; the counter and banquette read as used.

changes.problem: The terrazzo on the floor and the counter front reads as carpet or cork, not honed stone.

evidence.measured: counter front lum_median 20, saturated red and green flecks at 1:1; floor [290,680,800,800] median 47 with noisy grain and no reflection

change.setting: the terrazzo's chip size and ground tone
change.from: fine noisy chips (floor), large saturated multicoloured chips (counter)
change.to: a warm grey ground with 8 to 20 mm chips in muted marble tones (cream, grey, rust), honed roughness about 0.25 so the lights and stools reflect softly

changes.expected: The floor shows soft reflections of the stools and the foot line; the counter front reads as stone.

changes.problem: The porch is lit by one hot graze at the top that falls off to mud, and a stray diagonal haze shaft crosses the band.

change.from: graze 0.5 W/m2 at the top; haze 0.006 per m
change.to: graze 0.3 W/m2 spread to the full height of the baffle; haze 0.003 per m, or remove the source that makes the diagonal shaft

changes.expected: The porch and baffle read evenly with a gentle falloff, with no unexplained beam.

changes.problem: Repeated identical props (four stools, four tables, matching glasses) give away the render.

evidence.measured: four identical tables in a straight row; stools [180,570,445,800] identical with even spacing

change.to: rotate and offset the stools slightly, give one table a candle or a record, vary the glasses (a tumbler, a coupe, an empty glass), and drape the throw with real folds

changes.expected: A lived-in arrangement with no visible copy and paste.

changes.problem: The right wall and banquette sit in an undifferentiated dark with no pool.

evidence.measured: lum_median 17.6, a featureless plane; banquette [975,505,1200,700] median 21

change.to: 55 W, 26 deg, with the plaster's tone a touch warmer so its texture reads at the top of each pool

changes.expected: Soft scallops of light on the lime plaster above the banquette and on the leather, so the right side reads as cozy rather than empty.

out_of_scope.request: Show the EARF Tropos pair or a Core or Hemisphere lamp in this frame, so the one saturated colour comes from an EARF product
out_of_scope.why: The products are fixed as placed (the pair is inside the lantern). A camera move that sees through the porch, or a lamp on the counter, would need the owner's decision on placement

out_of_scope.request: Give the porch a reveal, a handle or a visible threshold so it reads as a sound lock rather than flat doors
out_of_scope.why: The porch's design is fixed architecture; only its oak tone and finish may change

out_of_scope.request: Remove or rethink the hard diagonal shadow on the slatted baffle if it comes from the porch or the lantern's geometry
out_of_scope.why: If an architectural element casts it, changing it would change the drawn architecture
